question: How do structural modifications of gold surfaces influence the band structure and alignment of seven-armchair graphene nanoribbons?
answer: Reshaping of the gold surface, including step-edge modifications and a missing row reconstruction, occurs during high-temperature growth of seven-armchair graphene nanoribbons (7-AGNRs). This reconstructed surface promotes 7-AGNR alignment along two preferred directions, enabling detailed characterization of their electronic band structure.

### Task 1: Summarize the purpose of the paper
The paper investigates the synthesis and electronic properties of seven-armchair graphene nanoribbons (7-AGNRs) grown on a vicinal gold surface (Au(16 14 15)) through on-surface chemistry. The study focuses on understanding how the substrate's step-edge reshaping and reconstruction during the growth process influence the alignment and band structure of the nanoribbons. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), the authors identify and characterize the energy and effective mass of the occupied frontier band of 7-AGNRs, validating theoretical predictions.

3. How do the structural modifications of the substrate impact the electronic band structure of 7-AGNRs?
